style.vernacular: Nordic city of timber and brick: weatherboarded wooden houses painted falu red, ochre yellow, white or grey with white window frames and gable roofs; 19th-century yellow-plaster and brick apartment blocks in the centre; 1930s Functionalism (funkis) in white render and brick; post-war limestone-brick and raw-concrete blocks; glass and timber contemporary buildings at Bjorvika and in suburbs such as Lorenskog. Roofs are dark concrete tile, slate, sheet metal, or green copper on civic buildings, among spruce, pine and birch.
style.ornament: Plain gable-roofed wooden houses with white window surrounds and corner boards; Swiss chalet and dragon-style gables with carved bargeboards on older villas; Functionalist white boxes with ribbon windows and flat roofs; green copper roofs and spires on civic buildings and churches; exposed oak and larch cladding on contemporary buildings.

sources.what: wood as main material with weatherboarded walls; neoclassical, Swiss chalet, dragon style, Jugendstil, Functionalism, brutalism in raw concrete; Oslo City Hall as key Functionalist example
contemporary Oslo-region buildings use wood, metal and glass (oak-clad pier)
